abstract: The International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration (INSDC; http://www.insdc.org/) provides global infrastructure for the collection, preservation, and dissemination of nucleotide sequence data through its three member organizations. As the collaboration approaches four decades of three-way data exchange, continued growth in both the volume and geographic distribution of data is creating new challenges. Cumulative volume now stands at over 75 PB, having doubled approximately every 2.5 years over the past decade. Data reuse is extensively demonstrated by the 39 055 publications citing INSDC records in the 12 months to August 2026. The INSDC has established a new governance structure and a formal pathway for membership, supported by minimal technical specifications that enable independently developed systems to interoperate. Prospect members are now progressing through this pathway. The collaboration is also responding to an evolving policy landscape, which needs to be balanced with its founding commitment to free and unrestricted access. Looking ahead, the INSDC is exploring more scalable approaches to data storage and federation, strengthening approaches to attribution and reuse, and considering applications of artificial intelligence for metadata enrichment and submission support. Altogether, these developments aim to sustain an open, global, and interoperable nucleotide sequence archive.

summary: INSDC reports its global nucleotide sequence archive now exceeds 75 PB, with new governance, a membership pathway, and planned AI-assisted metadata work.
title: The International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration (INSDC): sustaining open sequence data at global scale.
